At the beginning of your upkeep, sacrifice this enchantment unless you pay {W}{W}.
Whenever a red creature or spell deals damage, this enchantment deals that much damage to that creature's or spell's controller.

cards.name: Lifetap
cards.text: Whenever a Forest an opponent controls becomes tapped, you gain 1 life.
cards.flavor:
"Keep a green tree in your heart and perhaps the singing bird will come."
—Chinese proverb

cards.name: Living Artifact
cards.text:
Enchant artifact
Whenever you're dealt damage, put that many vitality counters on this Aura.
At the beginning of your upkeep, you may remove a vitality counter from this Aura. If you do, you gain 1 life.

cards.name: Magical Hack
cards.text: Change the text of target spell or permanent by replacing all instances of one basic land type with another. (For example, you may change "swampwalk" to "plainswalk." This effect lasts indefinitely.)

cards.name: Marsh Viper
cards.text: Whenever this creature deals damage to a player, that player gets two poison counters. (A player with ten or more poison counters loses the game.)
cards.flavor:
"And the seraphs sob at vermin fangs
In human gore imbued."
—Edgar Allan Poe, "The Conqueror Wurm"

cards.name: Mind Bomb
cards.text: Each player may discard up to three cards. Mind Bomb deals damage to each player equal to 3 minus the number of cards they discarded this way.

cards.name: Mind Ravel
cards.text:
Target player discards a card.
Draw a card at the beginning of the next turn's upkeep.
cards.flavor: An end to reason, an end to order. Forget all that has been.

cards.name: Mole Worms
cards.text:
You may choose not to untap this creature during your untap step.
{T}: Tap target land. It doesn't untap during its controller's untap step for as long as this creature remains tapped.

cards.name: Murk Dwellers
cards.text: Whenever this creature attacks and isn't blocked, it gets +2/+0 until end of combat.
cards.flavor: When Raganorn unsealed the catacombs, he found more than the dead and their treasures.

cards.name: Pikemen
cards.text: First strike; banding (Any creatures with banding, and up to one without, can attack in a band. Bands are blocked as a group. If any creatures with banding you control are blocking or being blocked by a creature, you divide that creature's combat damage, not its controller, among any of the creatures it's being blocked by or is blocking.)
cards.flavor:
"As the cavalry bore down, we faced them with swords drawn and pikes hidden in the grass at our feet. 'Don't lift your pikes 'til I give the word,' I said."
—Maeveen O'Donagh,
*Memoirs of a Soldier*

cards.name: Pit Scorpion
cards.text: Whenever this creature deals damage to a player, that player gets a poison counter. (A player with ten or more poison counters loses the game.)
cards.flavor: Sometimes the smallest nuisance can be the greatest pain.

cards.name: Plague Rats
cards.text: Plague Rats's power and toughness are each equal to the number of creatures named Plague Rats on the battlefield.
cards.flavor:
"Should you a Rat to madness tease Why ev'n a Rat may plague you . . . ."
—Samuel Coleridge, "Recantation"

cards.name: Primordial Ooze
cards.text:
This creature attacks each combat if able.
At the beginning of your upkeep, put a +1/+1 counter on this creature. Then you may pay {X}, where X is the number of +1/+1 counters on it. If you don't, tap this creature and it deals X damage to you.

cards.name: Prismatic Ward
cards.text:
Enchant creature
As this Aura enters, choose a color.
Prevent all damage that would be dealt to enchanted creature by sources of the chosen color.

cards.name: Reef Pirates
cards.text: Whenever this creature deals damage to an opponent, that player mills a card.
cards.flavor: Relentless as the tides, souls dark as a moonless night. Bloodshed on their minds, and greed burning in their hearts like molten gold.

cards.name: Repentant Blacksmith
cards.text: Protection from red
cards.flavor:
"For my confession they burned me with fire / And found that I was for endurance made."
—*The Arabian Nights*,
trans. Haddawy

cards.name: Sand Silos
cards.text:
This land enters tapped.
You may choose not to untap this land during your untap step.
At the beginning of your upkeep, if this land is tapped, put a storage counter on it.
{T}, Remove any number of storage counters from this land: Add {U} for each storage counter removed this way.

cards.name: Serra Paladin
cards.text:
{T}: Prevent the next 1 damage that would be dealt to any target this turn.
{1}{W}{W}, {T}: Target creature gains vigilance until end of turn.
cards.flavor:
One light, one blade, one purpose.
—Vow of the Serra Paladins

cards.name: Sleight of Mind
cards.text: Change the text of target spell or permanent by replacing all instances of one color word with another. (For example, you may change "target black spell" to "target blue spell." This effect lasts indefinitely.)

cards.name: Sorceress Queen
cards.text: {T}: Target creature other than this creature has base power and toughness 0/2 until end of turn.
cards.flavor:
"We have always counted time with sand; this pinch is your meaningless life."
—Nailah, self-proclaimed Queen of Rabiah

cards.name: Soul Barrier
cards.text: Whenever an opponent casts a creature spell, this enchantment deals 2 damage to that player unless they pay {2}.
cards.flavor:
"The Soul selects her own Society—
Then—shuts the Door—"
—Emily Dickinson,
"The Soul selects her own Society"

cards.name: Tarpan
cards.text: When this creature dies, you gain 1 life.
cards.flavor:
"A good tarpan will serve you, faithful and true. A bad one will kick you in the head."
—General Jarkeld, the Arctic Fox

cards.name: The Brute
cards.text:
Enchant creature
Enchanted creature gets +1/+0.
{R}{R}{R}: Regenerate enchanted creature.
cards.flavor: After years of being bullied, Fergo reaped the benefits of his newfound strength: he never met a man he didn't want to fight.

cards.name: Touch of Death
cards.text:
Touch of Death deals 1 damage to target player or planeswalker. You gain 1 life.
Draw a card at the beginning of the next turn's upkeep.
cards.flavor:
"What was yours is mine. Your land, your people, and now your life."
—Lim-Dûl, the Necromancer

cards.name: Truce
cards.text: Each player may draw up to two cards. For each card less than two a player draws this way, that player gains 2 life.
cards.flavor:
Not all victories require defeat.
—Onean idiom

cards.name: Updraft
cards.text:
Target creature gains flying until end of turn.
Draw a card at the beginning of the next turn's upkeep.
cards.flavor:
"Come one, come all! this rock shall fly From its firm base as soon as I."
—Sir Walter Scott, "The Lady of the Lake"

cards.name: Urza's Avenger
cards.text: {0}: This creature gets -1/-1 and gains your choice of banding, flying, first strike, or trample until end of turn. (Any creatures with banding, and up to one without, can attack in a band. Bands are blocked as a group. If any creatures with banding you control are blocking or being blocked by a creature, you divide that creature's combat damage, not its controller, among any of the creatures it's being blocked by or is blocking.)
cards.flavor: Unable to settle on just one design, Urza decided to create one versatile being.

cards.name: Venom
cards.text:
Enchant creature
Whenever enchanted creature blocks or becomes blocked by a non-Wall creature, destroy the other creature at end of combat.
cards.flavor:
"I told him it was just a flesh wound, but the next time I looked at him, poor Tadhg was dead and gone."
—Maeveen O'Donagh,
*Memoirs of a Soldier*

cards.name: Wall of Brambles
cards.text:
Defender (This creature can't attack.)
{G}: Regenerate this creature.
cards.flavor:
Sleeping in brambles
—Elven phrase meaning "plagued by guilt"

cards.name: Wolverine Pack
cards.text: Rampage 2 (Whenever this creature becomes blocked, it gets +2/+2 until end of turn for each creature blocking it beyond the first.)
cards.flavor:
"Give them great meals of beef and iron and steel, they will eat like wolves and fight like devils."
—William Shakespeare, *King Henry V*

cards.name: Zephyr Falcon
cards.text: Flying, vigilance
cards.flavor: Although greatly prized among falconers, the zephyr falcon is capricious and not easily tamed.

cards.name: Faerie Dragon
cards.text:
Flying
{1}{G}{G}: Play a random effect.

cards.name: Gem Bazaar

{T}: Add to your mana pool one mana of the color last chosen. Then choose a random color.

cards.name: Goblin Polka Band

Whenever a non-black creature is put into any graveyard from play, put a husk counter on Necropolis of Azar.
{5}, Remove a husk counter from Necropolis of Azar: Put a Spawn of Azar token into play. Treat this token as a black creature with a random power and toughness, each no less than 1 and no greater than 3, that has swampwalk.

Flying
During your upkeep, Prismatic Dragon becomes a random color permanently.
{2}: Prismatic Dragon becomes a random color permanently.

When Rainbow Knights comes into play, it gains protection from a random color permanently.
{1}: First strike until end of turn.
{W}{W}: +0/+0, +1/+0 or +2/+0 until end of turn chosen at random.

cards.name: Aswan Jaguar
cards.text:
When Aswan Jaguar comes into play, choose a random creature type from those in target opponent's deck.
{G}{G}, {T}: Bury target creature of the chosen type.

cards.name: Arrogant Vampire
cards.text: Flying
cards.flavor: Charm and grace may hide a foul heart.

cards.name: Assassin's Blade
cards.text:
Cast this spell only during the declare attackers step and only if you've been attacked this step.
Destroy target nonblack attacking creature.

cards.name: Capricious Sorcerer

cards.name: Charging Bandits
cards.text: Whenever this creature attacks, it gets +2/+0 until end of turn.
cards.flavor: The fear in their victims' eyes is their most cherished reward.

cards.name: Cloak of Feathers
cards.text:
Target creature gains flying until end of turn.
Draw a card.
cards.flavor: A thousand feathers from a thousand birds, sewn with magic and song.

cards.name: Cloud Pirates
cards.text:
Flying
This creature can block only creatures with flying.

cards.name: Command of Unsummoning
cards.text:
Cast this spell only during the declare attackers step and only if you've been attacked this step.
Return one or two target attacking creatures to their owner's hand.

cards.name: Craven Knight
cards.text: This creature can't block.
cards.flavor: "I say victory is better than honor."

cards.name: Cruel Fate
cards.text: Look at the top five cards of target opponent's library. Put one of those cards into that player's graveyard and the rest on top of their library in any order.

cards.name: Cruel Tutor
cards.text: Search your library for a card, then shuffle and put that card on top. You lose 2 life.
cards.flavor: The more you pay for the lesson, the better you'll remember it.

cards.name: Deep-Sea Serpent
cards.text: This creature can't attack unless defending player controls an Island.
cards.flavor: Sailors fear the deep-sea serpent; others thank the gods it has no legs.

cards.name: Defiant Stand
cards.text:
Cast this spell only during the declare attackers step and only if you've been attacked this step.
Target creature gets +1/+3 until end of turn. Untap that creature.

cards.name: Desert Drake
cards.text: Flying
cards.flavor: Never doubt a dragon just because of its size.

cards.name: Djinn of the Lamp
cards.text: Flying
cards.flavor: Once they learn the trick of carrying their own lamps, they never touch the ground again.

cards.name: Dread Charge
cards.text: Black creatures you control can't be blocked this turn except by black creatures.
cards.flavor:
"As equal were their souls, so equal was their fate."
—John Dryden, "Ode to Mrs. Anne Killigrew"

cards.name: Final Strike
cards.text:
As an additional cost to cast this spell, sacrifice a creature.
Final Strike deals damage to target opponent or planeswalker equal to the sacrificed creature's power.

cards.name: Fire Snake
cards.text: When this creature dies, destroy target land.
cards.flavor: The snake's final thrashings only spread the fire within it.

cards.name: Fleet-Footed Monk
cards.text: This creature can't be blocked by creatures with power 2 or greater.
cards.flavor: "Hesitation is for the faithless. My belief lends me speed."

cards.name: Fruition
cards.text: You gain 1 life for each Forest on the battlefield.
cards.flavor: Come to these woods and suffer no pain; you've burdens to lose and new life to gain.

cards.name: Keen-Eyed Archers
cards.text: Reach (This creature can block creatures with flying.)
cards.flavor: "If it has wings, shoot it. If it doesn't, shoot it anyway."

cards.name: King's Assassin
cards.text: {T}: Destroy target tapped creature. Activate only during your turn, before attackers are declared.
cards.flavor: Fear is as effective a weapon as the blade.

cards.name: Mercenary Knight
cards.text: When this creature enters, sacrifice it unless you discard a creature card.

cards.name: Mind Knives
cards.text: Target opponent discards a card at random.
cards.flavor: To dodge the unerring knife, one must be free of thought.

cards.name: Mobilize
cards.text: Untap all creatures you control.
cards.flavor: A rested mind is the sharpest weapon.

cards.name: Noxious Toad
cards.text: When this creature dies, each opponent discards a card.

cards.name: Omen
cards.text:
Look at the top three cards of your library, then put them back in any order. You may shuffle.
Draw a card.

cards.name: Plant Elemental
cards.text: When this creature enters, sacrifice it unless you sacrifice a Forest.

cards.name: Raging Cougar
cards.text: Haste
cards.flavor: Mountaineers quickly learn to travel with their spears always pointed up.

cards.name: Renewing Dawn
cards.text: You gain 2 life for each Mountain target opponent controls.
cards.flavor: Dawn brings a new day, and a new day brings hope.

cards.name: Sacred Knight
cards.text: This creature can't be blocked by black and/or red creatures.
cards.flavor: "No flame, no horror can sway me from my cause."

cards.name: Scorching Winds
cards.text:
Cast this spell only during the declare attackers step and only if you've been attacked this step.
Scorching Winds deals 1 damage to each attacking creature.

cards.name: Sorcerous Sight
cards.text:
Look at target opponent's hand.
Draw a card.
cards.flavor: Do not react; anticipate.

cards.name: Starlit Angel
cards.text: Flying
cards.flavor: To soar as high as hope, to dive as swift as justice.

cards.name: Stern Marshal
cards.text: {T}: Target creature gets +2/+2 until end of turn. Activate only during your turn, before attackers are declared.

cards.name: Taunt
cards.text: During target player's next turn, creatures that player controls attack you if able.

cards.name: Temporary Truce
cards.text: Each player may draw up to two cards. For each card less than two a player draws this way, that player gains 2 life.

cards.name: Thundering Wurm
cards.text: When this creature enters, sacrifice it unless you discard a land card.

cards.name: Treetop Defense
cards.text:
Cast this spell only during the declare attackers step and only if you've been attacked this step.
Creatures you control gain reach until end of turn. (They can block creatures with flying.)

cards.name: Undying Beast
cards.text: When this creature dies, put it on top of its owner's library.

cards.name: Valorous Charge
cards.text: White creatures get +2/+0 until end of turn.
cards.flavor: Stand in the way of truth at your peril.

cards.name: Vampiric Feast
cards.text: Vampiric Feast deals 4 damage to any target and you gain 4 life.
cards.flavor: It's not always gold the thief is after.

cards.name: Vampiric Touch
cards.text: Vampiric Touch deals 2 damage to target opponent or planeswalker and you gain 2 life.
cards.flavor: A touch, not comforting, but of death.

cards.name: Virtue's Ruin
cards.text: Destroy all white creatures.
cards.flavor: All must fall, and those who stand highest fall hardest.

cards.name: Wall of Granite
cards.text: Defender (This creature can't attack.)
cards.flavor: The wisest man builds his house *behind* the rock.

cards.name: Warrior's Charge
cards.text: Creatures you control get +1/+1 until end of turn.
cards.flavor: It is not the absence of fear that makes a warrior, but its domination.

cards.name: Willow Dryad
cards.text: Forestwalk (This creature can't be blocked as long as defending player controls a Forest.)
cards.flavor: Some think that dryads are the dreams of trees.

cards.name: Ashnod
cards.text: Whenever a creature deals damage to you, destroy it.
cards.flavor: Ashnod served as Mishra's confidante while he led Fallaji weapons development before the Brothers' War. Whereas Mishra works in metals and stone, however, Ashnod works in living flesh. She sees all living things as prototype machines; her "improvements" to them make her as feared by allies as by enemies.

cards.name: Barrin
cards.text: Sacrifice a permanent: Return target creature to its owner's hand.
cards.flavor: An old and powerful wizard living on the mysterious isle of Tolaria, Barrin is the teacher who trained the young Ertai. He is also Hanna's father, but for reasons known only to the two of them neither acknowledges the other—or their strained relationship.

cards.name: Crovax
cards.text: Whenever a creature you control deals damage to a creature or player, you gain 1 life.
cards.flavor: How does one escape a curse? For Crovax, a wealthy noble, the answer may lie in joining the crew of the *Weatherlight* as they seek to rescue their abducted captain Sisay. Secretly, he hopes in his journeys to find Selenia, the angelic being who abandoned him and his family years ago.

cards.name: Eladamri
cards.text: {0}: The next 1 damage that would be dealt to target creature you control is dealt to you instead.
cards.flavor: Proud, shrewd, and charismatic, Eladamri has a commitment to his people that is absolute. The guerilla war he wages against Volrath has convinced him that the only way to liberate the Skyshroud elves is to lead *all* Rath's refugees to freedom. So be it.

cards.name: Ertai
cards.text: Creatures you control have hexproof. (They can't be the targets of spells or abilities your opponents control.)
cards.flavor: After serving his apprenticeship under Barrin of Tolaria, Ertai graced the *Weatherlight* crew with his presence as the ship's "resident" wizard. He realizes that few recognize his greatness—but then how could they, when they lack his insight and wisdom?

cards.name: Gerrard
cards.text: At the beginning of your draw step, draw an additional card.
cards.flavor: Soldier. Adventurer. Heir to the Legacy. Gerrard has, over the years, traveled much of Dominaria in search of fortune and glory. Now, after serving nobly in the Benalish army, he has returned to the *Weatherlight* to serve as captain in Sisay's absence and to take up the battle against the Lord of the Wastes.

cards.name: Gix
cards.text: {3}: Return target creature card from your graveyard to your hand.
cards.flavor: Through ruthlessness and raw ambition, Gix rose through the Phyrexian regime to the exalted rank of praetor. Even while overseeing many of Phyrexia's most important undertakings, Gix continues his own quest for supremacy . . . for in Phyrexia, the weak become fodder for the strong.

cards.name: Greven il-Vec
cards.text: Whenever a creature you control deals damage to a creature, destroy the other creature. It can't be regenerated.
cards.flavor: As a ruthless leader for Volrath, Greven *il*-Vec serves his lord by commanding the flying ship *Predator*. Greven has attained his powerful rank through a series of underhanded schemes and assassinations, the majority of which were blessed by Volrath himself.

cards.name: Hanna
cards.text: Spells you cast cost {1} less to cast.
cards.flavor: Educated in Argive and highly knowledgeable in the field of artifacts, this expert navigator of the *Weatherlight* believes that scholarship does not necessarily lead to understanding. Her diligence in pursuing both is her greatest asset.

cards.name: Karn
cards.text: Each noncreature artifact you control is an artifact creature with power and toughness each equal to its mana value.
cards.flavor: Both part of the Legacy and an individual in his own right, the silver golem Karn is haunted by a single, terrible incident: while serving to protect the young Gerrard, Karn accidentally took the life of another. Wakened from years spent as a statue, the golem has vowed to never kill again as he rejoins Gerrard.

cards.name: Lyna
cards.text: Creatures you control have shadow. (They can block and be blocked only by creatures with shadow.)
cards.flavor: One of the few Soltari who can cross the shadow barrier, Lyna serves as an emissary to the outside world. A quick thinker and convincing speaker, she does whatever she can to lead her people out of the shadows and into substance.

cards.name: Maraxus
cards.text: Creatures you control get +1/+0.
cards.flavor: Too chaotic for even the other warlords of Keld, Maraxus has devoted himself to serving as a hired killer for the sinister Volrath. A man fond of his work, he's more than willing to put in those extra hours needed to perfect his craft.

cards.name: Mirri
cards.text: If a basic land you control is tapped for mana, it produces mana of a color of your choice instead of any other type.
cards.flavor: Mirri and Gerrard have been the best of friends since they trained together under the maro-sorcerer Multani. A fierce and agile warrior, she rejoined Gerrard aboard the *Weatherlight* as his unofficial first mate shortly after he assumed command of the flying ship.

cards.name: Mishra
cards.text: If a creature you control would deal damage, it deals double that damage instead.
cards.flavor: Both complement and antithesis to his older brother Urza, Mishra also mastered the intricacies of artifice. It was Mishra's strength that first gave rise to the massive Phyrexian war engines on Dominaria, and it was his weakness that pushed him, Urza, and Dominaria itself to the point of annihilation.

cards.name: Multani
cards.text: Creatures you control get +X/+0, where X is the number of cards in your hand.
cards.flavor: In mentoring apprentice mages, the forest spirit Multani teaches each to respect nature while making use of its gifts. Multani taught Gerrard, Mirri, and Rofellos to hone their spellcasting in tandem with more physical disciplines so that both would be improved.

cards.name: Oracle
cards.text: {0}: Untap target attacking creature you control and remove it from combat.
cards.flavor: Known simply by her title, Oracle uses her gift of prophecy to aid her people. She believes Gerrard to be the *Korvecdal*, the one who will unite the people of Rath against Volrath's tyranny. Her only doubt is whether she will be strong enough to guide him to his destiny.

cards.name: Orim
cards.text: Creatures you control have reach.
cards.flavor: Trained in the Samite arts, Orim serves as the healer aboard the *Weatherlight*. She is quick with languages and was educated at the same Argivian university as Hanna. A student by nature, Orim keeps a diary of all her new discoveries—both physical and spiritual—during her travels.

cards.name: Rofellos
cards.text: Whenever a creature you control dies, draw a card.
cards.flavor: Gerrard's longtime friend and fellow student under the maro-sorcerer Multani, Rofellos is an excellent warrior and excellent company. Though adept at both magic and swordplay, he's far more comfortable with a flagon in his hand and a good companion at his side.

cards.name: Selenia
cards.text: Creatures you control have vigilance.
cards.flavor: Once a guardian of Crovax's estate, Selenia was freed from her magical bindings by the wealthy noble. Instead of remaining at his side, the angel chose to venture out into the world. For reasons unknown to Crovax, Selenia now serves the evil Volrath in his home realm of Rath.

cards.name: Serra
cards.text: Creatures you control get +0/+2.
cards.flavor: Named for a benevolent goddess at birth, Serra fulfilled the prophecy of that goddess's coming. As a planeswalker, she embodies white mana and helps whole civilizations develop while both directly and indirectly inspiring countless individuals to be steadfast and strong in the service of light.

cards.name: Sidar Kondo
cards.text: {3}: Target creature gets +3/+3 until end of turn.
cards.flavor: Kondo served as guardian to the infant Gerrard and raised him alongside his own son, Vuel. He taught both boys to be strong and to lead, but whereas Gerrard became a champion of honor, Vuel's bitterness led him to become an equally devastating force of malice.

cards.name: Sisay
cards.text: Whenever you tap a land for mana, add one mana of any type that land produced.
cards.flavor: While captain of the *Weatherlight*, Sisay undertook a quest for the Legacy, a collection of artifacts needed to defeat the Lord of the Wastes. She continued this quest even when Gerrard, heir to the Legacy, chose to abandon it. Sisay is devoted to the cause of good at whatever price.

cards.name: Sliver Queen, Brood Mother
cards.text: {3}: Create a 1/1 colorless Sliver creature token.
cards.flavor: Though long held captive beneath Volrath's stronghold, the sliver queen is actually freer than most of Rath's denizens. Her maternal instincts always take precedence—even when they conflict with the evincar's agenda—and through her numerous litters, she ranges across all of Rath.

cards.name: Squee
cards.text: Your opponents play with their hands revealed.
cards.flavor: The smartest—and only—goblin cabin boy aboard the *Weatherlight*, Squee has learned that intelligence and common sense are very different things. This matters little, however, since he has neither. Fortunately, he doesn't know what he's missing.

cards.name: Starke
cards.text: At the beginning of your draw step, you may draw an additional card. If you do, put a card from your hand on the bottom of your library.
cards.flavor: Starke believes in situational ethics—the situation determines the ethics. He's switched sides so often that he has become everyone's ally yet no one's friend. This former merchant of Rath accompanies the *Weatherlight* crew on their journey to his home world.

cards.name: Tahngarth
cards.text: Creatures you control have haste.
cards.flavor: Tahngarth, first mate of the *Weatherlight* under Sisay, knows that there are really only two forms of life: the ugly ones and the minotaurs. A narcissist, he considers the condition of his hide as important as the accuracy of his blade.

cards.name: Takara
cards.text: Sacrifice a creature: Takara deals 1 damage to any target.
cards.flavor: Takara banishes the shadow of her father's ignoble reputation through the dedication, plain speaking, and swift action of a warrior. By refusing Starke's path of self-interest and opportunism, she has learned what he never will know: the value of sacrifice for a worthy cause.

cards.name: Tawnos
cards.text: You may cast artifact, creature, and enchantment spells as though they had flash.
cards.flavor: Tawnos brings a childlike wonder and an inherent skill to Urza's studio and bridges the wizardry of the workshop with the grandeur of the royal court. His speed and flexibility quickly earned him promotion from apprentice to master artificer.

cards.name: Titania
cards.text: You may play an additional land on each of your turns.
cards.flavor: Voice of the Argoth forest, defender of its creatures, and enforcer of its laws, Titania is literally an aspect of the forest itself. Her power and her very existence are linked to the land: when the forest is healthy, Titania is ascendant. When Argoth suffers, Titania also bleeds.

cards.name: Urza
cards.text: {3}: Urza deals 1 damage to any target.
cards.flavor: An artificer of unparalleled renown, Urza was a powerful cipher even before he was able to planeswalk. Seeing the world as a large, integrated machine is his greatest strength and weakness, enabling him to solve almost any problem but blinding him to his solutions' effects on others.

cards.name: Volrath

cards.name: Jakub Šlemr Bio
cards.text: Šlemr, a twenty-year-old computer analyst from Prague in the Czech Republic, said that he wasn't happy with his deck's 3—4 performance in the Standard (Type II) portion of the tournament. However, it came through for him in the elimination rounds. A black weenie deck at heart, it dips into all five colors. It also features a number of creatures that have an effect on entering play, like Man-o'-War, Uktabi Orangutan, and Nekrataal.

cards.name: Janosch Kühn Bio (1997)
cards.text: Kühn, a fifteen-year-old high-school student from Hanover, Germany, played a red, white, and blue deck with a balanced mix of speed and control. It uses cards like Incinerate and Swords to Plowshares to deal with opponents' fast creatures, while increasing the mana base with Thawing Glaciers. For late in the game, Disintegrate and Hammer of Bogardan are excellent finishing cards.

cards.name: Paul McCabe Bio
cards.text: McCabe, a nineteen-year-old college student from Toronto, Canada, played a fast red-blue attacking deck. The deck's main strategy is to put the opponent on the defensive, using a large number of inexpensive, efficient creatures such as Suq'Ata Lancer, Cloud Elemental, Ophidian, and Man-o'-War. It also makes good use of several "pitch" spells like Force of Will and Pyrokinesis.

cards.name: Svend Geertsen Bio
cards.text: Geertsen, a sixteen-year-old high-school student from Copenhagen, Denmark, played a mono-green deck known affectionately as "Señor Stompie." Of the eight finalists, Geertsen had the best record in the Standard (Type II) portion of the tournament, going 6—0—1. This deck is overloaded with fast green creatures, thirty-three in all. The only noncreature cards are Giant Growth, Bounty of the Hunt, and Winter Orb. The deck also exploits the interaction between Rogue Elephant, Harvest Worm, and Heart of Yavimaya.

cards.text: Though only fifteen years old, Ben Rubin has amassed quite an impressive tournament record. He placed second at Pro Tour™—Los Angeles and finished in the Top 16 at Grand Prix—San Francisco, his hometown. Ben played the archetypal mono-red weenie or Sligh deck at the 1998 Worlds. Although he prefers to play a more balanced deck, Rubin thought the aggressive Sligh would work well at this tournament. His deck consists of roughly one-third land, one-third direct damage, and one-third small aggressive creatures.

cards.name: Brian Hacker Bio
cards.text: Twenty-three-year-old professional Magic® player Brian Hacker of San Diego, California, thought he had a good chance of winning the finals with his white weenie deck. Hacker said his deck was well set up to defeat his opponents with its twenty-something aggressive creatures—including a number of shadow and en-Kor creatures. Unlike traditional white weenie decks, which rely on Armageddon as a major threat card, Hacker's deck uses Cataclysm, which he feels better complements the use of Empyrial Armor.

cards.name: Brian Selden Bio
cards.text: Brian Selden, a seventeen-year-old high school student from San Diego, California, says his deck revolves around the interaction between Survival of the Fittest and Recurring Nightmare. The former is used to put creatures into the graveyard and the latter can then bring them into play. With this combo, Selden is able to use his creatures to react to an opponent's threats. The deck also contains over twenty creatures, many of which have an effect when they enter play or perform some other useful function, such as the Spike Weaver. Unlike many similar decks, Selden's dips into blue, primarily for Lobotomy. He said this was the key to many of his victories.

cards.name: Randy Buehler Bio
cards.text: Although twenty-six-year-old professional Magic® player Randy Buehler of Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, didn't make the Top 8, he did finish with an impressive 6—1 record during the Standard portion of the World Championships. Buehler's Draw, Go deck is built for pure control with over twenty counters. He uses eight card-drawing spells to get to his counters more quickly and only four Stalking Stones and one Rainbow Efreet for offensive power. Buehler said he won some games without ever having to tap a land for mana on his own turn.

cards.flavor:
"And the flamingos said, 'Get out of our nest—we can't be seen with the likes of you!' So, the griffin ate them."
—Azeworai, "The Ugly Bird"

cards.name: Dense Foliage
cards.text: Creatures can't be the targets of spells.
cards.flavor:
"Big plants not only good for hidin', but full o' tasty bugs, too."
—Squee, goblin cabin hand

cards.name: Dragon Mask

cards.flavor:
"With no further options, I was forced to don the mask."
—Rashida Scalebane

cards.name: Dread of Night
cards.text: White creatures get -1/-1.
cards.flavor:
"These moonless, foreign skies keep me in thrall. Dark whispers echo in the night, and I cannot resist."
—Selenia, dark angel

cards.name: Ekundu Griffin
cards.text: Flying, first strike
cards.flavor:
"My goat was a small price to pay for the chance to see the hunting griffin dive and seize it."
—Suq'Ata trader

cards.name: Elven Cache
cards.text: Return target card from your graveyard to your hand.
cards.flavor: Elves know where to harvest the best of the forest, for they planted it there themselves.

cards.name: Ethereal Champion
cards.text: Pay 1 life: Prevent the next 1 damage that would be dealt to this creature this turn.
cards.flavor:
"If I have learned anything as a wizard it is this: never fight your own battles."
—Waffa, sorcerer of Nyomba

cards.name: Fallow Earth
cards.text: Put target land on top of its owner's library.
cards.flavor:
". . . and when the farmer awoke the next morning, all the seeds from his field were once again in their sacks."
—Afari, *Tales*

cards.name: Fatal Blow
cards.text: Destroy target creature that was dealt damage this turn. It can't be regenerated.
cards.flavor:
"What is crueler? To let a wound of the heart fester, or to simply cut it out?"
—Crovax

cards.name: Feast of the Unicorn
cards.text:
Enchant creature
Enchanted creature gets +4/+0.
cards.flavor:
"Could there be a fouler act? No doubt the baron knows of one."
—Autumn Willow

cards.name: Fit of Rage
cards.text: Target creature gets +3/+3 and gains first strike until end of turn.
cards.flavor:
"Anger is fleeting; remorse is eternal."
—Karn, silver golem

cards.name: Forbidden Crypt

If you would draw a card, return a card from your graveyard to your hand instead. If you can't, you lose the game.
If a card would be put into your graveyard from anywhere, exile that card instead.

cards.name: Forget
cards.text: Target player discards two cards, then draws as many cards as they discarded this way.

cards.name: Fyndhorn Brownie
cards.text: {2}{G}, {T}: Untap target creature.
cards.flavor:
"I've been insulted by drunks in a hundred inns, but never as skillfully or annoyingly as by those blasted brownies."
—General Jarkeld, the Arctic Fox

cards.name: Goblin Recruiter
cards.text: When this creature enters, search your library for any number of Goblin cards, reveal them, then shuffle and put those cards on top in any order.
cards.flavor: "Next!"

cards.name: Gravebane Zombie
cards.text: If this creature would die, put it on top of its owner's library instead.

cards.name: Harmattan Efreet
cards.text:
Flying
{1}{U}{U}: Target creature gains flying until end of turn.
cards.flavor:
"One moment I was walking along the beach, and the next I was high in the air, staring into a hideous smiling face."
—Tarub, Suq'Ata sailor

cards.name: Hero's Resolve
cards.text:
Enchant creature
Enchanted creature gets +1/+5.
cards.flavor:
"Destiny, chance, fate, fortune—they're all just ways of claiming your successes without claiming your failures."
—Gerrard of the *Weatherlight*

cards.name: Illicit Auction
cards.text: Each player may bid life for control of target creature. You start the bidding with a bid of 0. In turn order, each player may top the high bid. The bidding ends if the high bid stands. The high bidder loses life equal to the high bid and gains control of the creature. (This effect lasts indefinitely.)

cards.name: Insight
cards.text: Whenever an opponent casts a green spell, you draw a card.
cards.flavor:
"We can fight with you or against you. After my day, I'd prefer the former."
—Gerrard of the *Weatherlight*

cards.name: Lead Golem
cards.text: Whenever this creature attacks, it doesn't untap during its controller's next untap step.
cards.flavor: Slow and heavy swings the club.

cards.name: Library of Lat-Nam
cards.text:
An opponent chooses one —
• You draw three cards at the beginning of the next turn's upkeep.
• You search your library for a card, put that card into your hand, then shuffle.

cards.name: Light of Day
cards.text: Black creatures can't attack or block.
cards.flavor:
"I do not miss sunlight. The very memory of it burns my eyes."
—Volrath

cards.name: Lost Soul
cards.text: Swampwalk (This creature can't be blocked as long as defending player controls a Swamp.)
cards.flavor: Her hand gently beckons, she whispers your name—but those who go with her are never the same.

cards.name: Mesa Falcon
cards.text:
Flying
{1}{W}: This creature gets +0/+1 until end of turn.
cards.flavor:
"The faith of Serra is borne on wings of hope."
—Gulsen, abbey matron

cards.name: Mind Warp
cards.text: Look at target player's hand and choose X cards from it. That player discards those cards.
cards.flavor: The hardest of wizards can have the softest of minds.

cards.name: Mischievous Poltergeist
cards.text:
Flying
Pay 1 life: Regenerate this creature.
cards.flavor:
"The past is a ghost that haunts you from the moment it exists until the moment you don't."
—Gerrard of the *Weatherlight*

cards.name: Mountain Goat
cards.text: Mountainwalk (This creature can't be blocked as long as defending player controls a Mountain.)
cards.flavor: Only the heroic and the mad follow mountain goat trails.

cards.name: Mystic Compass
cards.text: {1}, {T}: Target land becomes the basic land type of your choice until end of turn.

cards.name: Painful Memories
cards.text: Look at target opponent's hand and choose a card from it. Put that card on top of that player's library.
cards.flavor:
"It is terrible how one brief action can live forever in memory."
—Jolrael

cards.name: Pearl Dragon
cards.text:
Flying
{1}{W}: This creature gets +0/+1 until end of turn.
cards.flavor:
"They knew Bantau was lost when, to hide the pearl he had found on the beach, he swallowed it—and soon grew wings."
—Hakim, Loreweaver

cards.name: Perish
cards.text: Destroy all green creatures. They can't be regenerated.
cards.flavor:
"There will come a time when the voices of soil and seedling will sing only laments."
—Oracle *en*-Vec

cards.name: Pestilence
cards.text:
At the beginning of the end step, if no creatures are on the battlefield, sacrifice this enchantment.
{B}: This enchantment deals 1 damage to each creature and each player.

cards.name: Pradesh Gypsies
cards.text: {1}{G}, {T}: Target creature gets -2/-0 until end of turn.
cards.flavor:
"A mysterious people indeed. Their origins are as secret as their traditions."
—Lord Magnus of Llanowar

cards.name: Resistance Fighter
cards.text: Sacrifice this creature: Prevent all combat damage target creature would deal this turn.
cards.flavor:
"My soldiers fought without hesitation, died without doubt."
—Sidar Jabari

cards.name: Segovian Leviathan
cards.text: Islandwalk (This creature can't be blocked as long as defending player controls an Island.)
cards.flavor:
"Leviathan, too! Can you catch him with a fish-hook or run a line round his tongue?"
—*The Bible*, Job 41:1

cards.name: Serenity
cards.text: At the beginning of your upkeep, destroy all artifacts and enchantments. They can't be regenerated.
cards.flavor:
"Just think of me as the storm before the calm."
—Gerrard of the *Weatherlight*

cards.name: Snake Basket
cards.text: {X}, Sacrifice this artifact: Create X 1/1 green Snake creature tokens. Activate only as a sorcery.
cards.flavor:
"Uh, does anyone have a flute?"
—Rana, Suq'Ata market fool

cards.name: Soldevi Sage
cards.text: {T}, Sacrifice two lands: Draw three cards, then discard one of them.
cards.flavor:
"To hide the truth is more than folly—it is fatal."
—Sorine Relicbane, Soldevi heretic

cards.name: Spitting Drake
cards.text:
Flying
{R}: This creature gets +1/+0 until end of turn. Activate only once each turn.
cards.flavor: It prefers its meals cooked.

cards.name: Talruum Minotaur
cards.text: Haste
cards.flavor:
Don't insult a Talruum unless your mount is swift.
—Suq'Ata saying

cards.name: Tariff
cards.text: Each player sacrifices the creature they control with the greatest mana value unless they pay that creature's mana cost. If two or more creatures a player controls are tied for greatest, that player chooses one.

cards.name: Tidal Surge
cards.text: Tap up to three target creatures without flying.
cards.flavor:
"It is nature that gives us our boundaries and nature that enforces them."
—Eladamri, Lord of Leaves

cards.name: Tranquil Grove
cards.text: {1}{G}{G}: Destroy all other enchantments.

cards.name: Uktabi Orangutan
cards.text: When this creature enters, destroy target artifact.
cards.flavor:
"Is it true that the apes wear furs of gold when they marry?"
—Rana, Suq'Ata market fool

cards.name: Unseen Walker

Forestwalk (This creature can't be blocked as long as defending player controls a Forest.)
{1}{G}{G}: Target creature gains forestwalk until end of turn.
cards.flavor:
"To pass through the jungle: silence, courtesy, ferocity, as the occasion demands."
—Kamau, "Proper Passage"

cards.name: Unyaro Griffin
cards.text:
Flying
Sacrifice this creature: Counter target red instant or sorcery spell.
cards.flavor: The griffin's shadow gives courage to the righteous and dread to the idle.

cards.name: Vertigo
cards.text: Vertigo deals 2 damage to target creature with flying. That creature loses flying until end of turn.
cards.flavor:
"I saw the wizard gesturing, but I didn't guess his plan until my aesthir cried out and went into a dive."
—Arna Kennerüd, skyknight

cards.name: Vitalize
cards.text: Untap all creatures you control.
cards.flavor:
"After waking to the magic of Llanowar, no dreams can compare."
—Mirri of the *Weatherlight*

cards.name: Waiting in the Weeds
cards.text: Each player creates a 1/1 green Cat creature token for each untapped Forest they control.
cards.flavor: The trees have ears, eyes, and teeth.

cards.name: Wand of Denial
cards.text: {T}: Look at the top card of target player's library. If it's a nonland card, you may pay 2 life. If you do, put it into that player's graveyard.
cards.flavor: You'll never miss what you never had.

cards.name: Warmth
cards.text: Whenever an opponent casts a red spell, you gain 2 life.
cards.flavor:
"Flame grows gentle with but a little distance."
—Orim, Samite healer

cards.name: Warthog
cards.text: Swampwalk (This creature can't be blocked as long as defending player controls a Swamp.)
cards.flavor:
"Too much work—it takes a long time to break them in, and more than a few recruits."
—Grebog, goblin swine-rider

cards.name: Alert Shu Infantry
cards.text: Vigilance
cards.flavor: Kongming's predecessor helped Liu Bei win the battle of Fancheng by recognizing and defeating Cao Ren's use of the dreaded "Eight Gold Locks" formation.

cards.name: Barbarian General
cards.text: Horsemanship (This creature can't be blocked except by creatures with horsemanship.)
cards.flavor:
"Barbarian tribes with their rulers are inferior to Chinese states without them."
—Confucius, *The Analects* (trans. Lau)

cards.name: Borrowing the East Wind
cards.text: Borrowing the East Wind deals X damage to each creature with horsemanship and each player.

cards.name: Broken Dam
cards.text: Tap one or two target creatures without horsemanship.
cards.flavor: Using nature to their advantage, wise Three Kingdoms generals often let dammed rivers loose to destroy their enemies.

cards.name: Burning Fields
cards.text: Burning Fields deals 5 damage to target opponent or planeswalker.
cards.flavor:
"In raiding and plundering, be like fire, in immovability like a mountain."
—Sun Tzu, *Art of War* (trans. Giles)

cards.name: Cao Cao, Lord of Wei
cards.text: {T}: Target opponent discards two cards. Activate only during your turn, before attackers are declared.

cards.name: Cao Ren, Wei Commander
cards.text:
Horsemanship (This creature can't be blocked except by creatures with horsemanship.)
When Cao Ren enters, you lose 3 life.
cards.flavor: Cao Cao's cousin, Cao Ren was known throughout the three kingdoms as the fiercest of warriors.

cards.name: Champion's Victory
cards.text:
Cast this spell only during the declare attackers step and only if you've been attacked this step.
Return target attacking creature to its owner's hand.

cards.name: Control of the Court
cards.text: Draw four cards, then discard three cards at random.
cards.flavor: "Power-hungry eunuchs, the curse of the dynasty, have thrown the masses of the people into the depths of misery."

cards.name: Council of Advisors
cards.text: When this creature enters, draw a card.
cards.flavor: Sun Quan's long and successful rule in the years 199 to 251 was due to his ability to choose and foster talented advisors and generals.

cards.name: Counterintelligence
cards.text: Return one or two target creatures to their owners' hands.
cards.flavor: Before the battle of Red Cliffs, a supposedly sleeping Zhou Yu allowed his old friend, a Wei advisor, to steal a planted letter forged as if from Wei's two best admirals.

cards.name: Cunning Advisor
cards.text: {T}: Target opponent discards a card. Activate only during your turn, before attackers are declared.

cards.name: Deception
cards.text: Target opponent discards two cards.
cards.flavor: Believing they wrote the forged letter that had been stolen from Zhou Yu, Cao Cao rashly executed his two best admirals for treason.

cards.name: Desert Sandstorm
cards.text: Desert Sandstorm deals 1 damage to each creature.
cards.flavor: While pursuing the remnants of Yuan Shao's forces into the Wuhan Desert, Cao Cao was temporarily turned back by a fierce sandstorm.

cards.name: Diaochan, Artful Beauty
cards.text: {T}: Destroy target creature of your choice, then destroy target creature of an opponent's choice. Activate only during your turn, before attackers are declared.

cards.name: Empty City Ruse
cards.text: Target opponent skips all combat phases of their next turn.
cards.flavor: Out of time and options, Kongming was forced to bluff at Xicheng. He tricked an army of 150,000 Wei by leaving the city gates open and calmly playing the zither.

cards.name: Eunuchs' Intrigues
cards.text: Target opponent chooses a creature they control. Other creatures they control can't block this turn.
cards.flavor: Taking control of powerful court positions one by one, eunuchs eventually brought on the fall of the Han dynasty, leading to the chaos of the Three Kingdoms.

cards.name: False Mourning
cards.text: Put target card from your graveyard on top of your library.
cards.flavor: Zhou Yu, Sun Ce, and other famous generals feigned their deaths in order to later surprise their opponents.

cards.name: Fire Bowman
cards.text: Sacrifice this creature: It deals 1 damage to any target. Activate only during your turn, before attackers are declared.

cards.name: Flanking Troops
cards.text: Whenever this creature attacks, you may tap target creature.
cards.flavor: Following the battle of Redcliffs, both Liu Bei and Sun Quan coveted the province of Jingzhou. After Sun Quan's troops failed to capture it, Liu Bei's succeeded.

cards.name: Huang Zhong, Shu General
cards.text: Huang Zhong can't be blocked by more than one creature.
cards.flavor: "Virile in war, he kept the north in fear; His prodigies subdued the western sphere."

cards.name: Imperial Edict
cards.text: Target opponent chooses a creature they control. Destroy that creature.
cards.flavor: Frustrated with Cao Cao's control of the imperial court, Emperor Xian secretly issued an edict condemning him, using his own blood as ink.

cards.name: Kongming's Contraptions
cards.text: {T}: This creature deals 2 damage to target attacking creature. Activate only during the declare attackers step and only if you've been attacked this step.

cards.name: Lady Sun
cards.text: {T}: Return Lady Sun and another target creature to their owners' hands. Activate only during your turn, before attackers are declared.
cards.flavor: Sister to Sun Quan and wife to Liu Bei, Lady Sun often felt her loyalty to both tested.

cards.name: Lady Zhurong, Warrior Queen
cards.text: Horsemanship (This creature can't be blocked except by creatures with horsemanship.)
cards.flavor:
"A man, and such a fool! I, a woman, will fight them for you."
—Lady Zhurong to her husband Meng Huo, before leading an army against the Shu

cards.name: Lu Su, Wu Advisor
cards.text: {T}: Draw a card. Activate only during your turn, before attackers are declared.
cards.flavor: Lu Su served as an intermediary between the Wu and Shu kingdoms until Zhou Yu's death in 210, when he became Wu's supreme commander.

cards.name: Ma Chao, Western Warrior
cards.text:
Horsemanship (This creature can't be blocked except by creatures with horsemanship.)
Whenever Ma Chao attacks alone, it can't be blocked this combat.

cards.name: Marshaling the Troops
cards.text: Tap any number of untapped creatures you control. You gain 4 life for each creature tapped this way.

cards.name: Mountain Bandit
cards.text: Haste
cards.flavor: Penniless and far from home, many former Yellow Scarves and other soldiers became bandits to survive.

cards.name: Mystic Denial
cards.text: Counter target creature or sorcery spell.

cards.name: Pang Tong, "Young Phoenix"
cards.text: {T}: Target creature gets +0/+2 until end of turn. Activate only during your turn, before attackers are declared.
cards.flavor: ". . . It was Pang Tong's boat-connecting scheme That let Zhou Yu accomplish his great deed."

cards.name: Poison Arrow
cards.text: Destroy target nonblack creature. You gain 3 life.
cards.flavor: In ancient China, not wearing armor could be a fatal mistake. Guan Yu, Zhou Yu, Sun Ce, and other heros were struck by poison arrows.

cards.name: Preemptive Strike
cards.text: Counter target creature spell.

cards.name: Rally the Troops
cards.text:
Cast this spell only during the declare attackers step and only if you've been attacked this step.
Untap all creatures you control.

cards.name: Ravaging Horde
cards.text: When this creature enters, destroy target land.
cards.flavor: Upon his return to the capitol after taking soldiers to loot a nearby peaceful town, the prime minister, Dong Zhou, boasted of it as a victory over bandits.

cards.name: Renegade Troops
cards.text: Haste
cards.flavor: "Across the land rebellions seethed and swarmed / As vicious war lords swooped down on all sides."

cards.name: Return to Battle
cards.text: Return target creature card from your graveyard to your hand.
cards.flavor: "Swallowing his eye, the valiant Xiahou Dun fought on; / But Cao Cao's vanguard, its commander wounded, could not hold out for long."

cards.name: Riding Red Hare
cards.text: Target creature gets +3/+3 and gains horsemanship until end of turn. (It can't be blocked except by creatures with horsemanship.)
cards.flavor: One of the greatest steeds in the empire, Red Hare could travel a thousand *li* a day and climb hills as if running on flat ground.

cards.name: Sage's Knowledge
cards.text: Return target sorcery card from your graveyard to your hand.
cards.flavor:
"Those who know do not talk. Those who talk do not know."
—Lao Tzu, *Tao Te Ching*
(trans. Feng and English)

cards.name: Shu Defender
cards.text: Whenever this creature blocks, it gets +0/+2 until end of turn.
cards.flavor: Confronting Cao Cao's army at Steepslope Bridge, Zhang Fei bellowed, "I am Zhang Fei of Yan! Who dares fight me to the death?" Cao Cao's army cowered and fled.

cards.name: Shu Farmer
cards.text: {T}: You gain 1 life. Activate only during your turn, before attackers are declared.
cards.flavor:
"The common folk are ceaselessly active. The fields are fertile and the soil productive, and neither flood nor drought plagues us."
—A Shu diplomat

cards.name: Shu Grain Caravan
cards.text: When this creature enters, you gain 2 life.
cards.flavor: Keeping a million-man army fed was no easy task. Grain and rice caravans were the lifeblood of the empire.

cards.name: Sima Yi, Wei Field Marshal
cards.text: Sima Yi's power is equal to the number of Swamps you control.
cards.flavor: Sima Yi fought for four generations of the Cao family before his own grandson became emperor and united the three kingdoms.

cards.name: Spring of Eternal Peace
cards.text: You gain 8 life.
cards.flavor: Bathing in this spring could cure ailments of body and mind alike.

cards.name: Stone Catapult
cards.text: {T}: Destroy target tapped nonblack creature. Activate only during your turn, before attackers are declared.

cards.name: Taoist Hermit
cards.text: Hexproof (This creature can't be the target of spells or abilities your opponents control.)
cards.flavor: Taoists chose to be hermits for many reasons, but all shared one unchanging goal: to follow the Tao.

cards.name: Taoist Mystic
cards.text: This creature can't be blocked by creatures with horsemanship.
cards.flavor: By appearing in places miles apart at the same time, Zuo Ci exhibited the mystic's ability to "shrink the land."

cards.name: Taunting Challenge
cards.text: All creatures able to block target creature this turn do so.
cards.flavor: Incensed by their opponents' unrelenting taunts, even wise generals were known to rashly lead their troops into battle—often to disastrous defeats.

cards.name: Trained Cheetah
cards.text: Whenever this creature becomes blocked, it gets +1/+1 until end of turn.
cards.flavor: "[King Mulu's cheetahs] came riding on the winds, charging, with fangs bared and claws flexed."

cards.name: Virtuous Charge
cards.text: Creatures you control get +1/+1 until end of turn.
cards.flavor: "The empire belongs to no one man but to all in the empire. He who has virtue shall possess it."

cards.name: Warrior's Stand
cards.text:
Cast this spell only during the declare attackers step and only if you've been attacked this step.
Creatures you control get +2/+2 until end of turn.

cards.name: Wei Ambush Force
cards.text: Whenever this creature attacks, it gets +2/+0 until end of turn.
cards.flavor: The battle of Puyang marked the beginning of the end for Lu Bu. He lost the city—and later his life—to Cao Cao.

cards.name: Wei Assassins
cards.text: When this creature enters, target opponent chooses a creature they control. Destroy that creature.

cards.name: Wei Scout
cards.text: Horsemanship (This creature can't be blocked except by creatures with horsemanship.)
cards.flavor:
"He will win who, prepared himself, waits to take the enemy unprepared."
—Sun Tzu, *Art of War* (trans. Giles)

cards.name: Wielding the Green Dragon
cards.text: Target creature gets +4/+4 until end of turn.
cards.flavor: Named for the eastern part of the sky, the source of energy and renewal, Guan Yu's crescent-moon blade weighed over 100 pounds.

cards.name: Wu Admiral
cards.text: This creature gets +1/+1 as long as an opponent controls an Island.
cards.flavor: The Wu kingdom's well-trained admirals were integral to the Southlands' victory at Red Cliffs as well as the kingdom's defense.

cards.name: Wu Light Cavalry
cards.text: Horsemanship (This creature can't be blocked except by creatures with horsemanship.)
cards.flavor: A cunning strategist, Cao Ren tricked Zhou Yu by letting him enter Nanjun. Zhou Yu thought he was capturing the city until Cao Ren's arrows rained down upon him.

cards.name: Wu Scout
cards.text:
Horsemanship (This creature can't be blocked except by creatures with horsemanship.)
When this creature enters, look at target opponent's hand.

cards.name: Wu Spy
cards.text: When this creature enters, look at the top two cards of target player's library. Put one of them into their graveyard.

cards.name: Xun Yu, Wei Advisor
cards.text: {T}: Target creature you control gets +2/+0 until end of turn. Activate only during your turn, before attackers are declared.
cards.flavor: "A splendid talent, admired of all men! His folly lay in serving Cao Cao's power."

cards.name: Yellow Scarves Cavalry
cards.text:
Horsemanship (This creature can't be blocked except by creatures with horsemanship.)
This creature can't block.

cards.name: Yellow Scarves General
cards.text:
Horsemanship (This creature can't be blocked except by creatures with horsemanship.)
This creature can't block.
cards.flavor: Zhang Jue, leader of the Yellow Scarves rebellion, was a Taoist master and tutored his soldiers in those arts.

cards.name: Yellow Scarves Troops
cards.text: This creature can't block.
cards.flavor: Over 500,000 commoners followed Zhang Jue, General of Heaven, in his attempt to overthrow the corrupt Han dynasty.

cards.name: Yuan Shao's Infantry
cards.text: Whenever this creature attacks alone, this creature can't be blocked this combat.

cards.name: Yuan Shao, the Indecisive
cards.text:
Horsemanship (This creature can't be blocked except by creatures with horsemanship.)
Each creature you control can't be blocked by more than one creature.

cards.name: Zhang He, Wei General
cards.text:
Horsemanship (This creature can't be blocked except by creatures with horsemanship.)
Whenever Zhang He attacks, each other creature you control gets +1/+0 until end of turn.

cards.name: Zhang Liao, Hero of Hefei
cards.text: Whenever Zhang Liao deals damage to an opponent, that opponent discards a card.

cards.name: Zhao Zilong, Tiger General
cards.text:
Horsemanship (This creature can't be blocked except by creatures with horsemanship.)
Whenever Zhao Zilong blocks, it gets +1/+1 until end of turn.
cards.flavor: Zhao Zilong was a brave and noble warrior. Twice he rescued Liu Bei's son, Liu Shan.

cards.name: Zhou Yu, Chief Commander
cards.text: Zhou Yu can't attack unless defending player controls an Island.
cards.flavor:
"After making me, Zhou Yu, did you have to make Kongming?"
—Zhou Yu crying to heaven on his deathbed

cards.name: Zhuge Jin, Wu Strategist
cards.text: {T}: Target creature can't be blocked this turn. Activate only during your turn, before attackers are declared.
cards.flavor: When Zhuge Jin proposed the marriage of Guan Yu's daugher and Sun Quan's heir, Guan Yu's arrogant refusal led to disaster.

cards.name: Zodiac Dog
cards.text: Mountainwalk (This creature can't be blocked as long as defending player controls a Mountain.)
cards.flavor: ". . . Jiang Wei alone still strove with might and main: / Nine times more he fought the north—in vain. . . ."

cards.name: Zodiac Goat
cards.text: Mountainwalk (This creature can't be blocked as long as defending player controls a Mountain.)
cards.flavor: ". . . Near death in Baidi, having reigned three years, / Bei sadly placed his son in Kongming's care. . . ."

cards.name: Zodiac Horse
cards.text: Islandwalk (This creature can't be blocked as long as defending player controls an Island.)
cards.flavor: ". . . 'First take Jingzhou, next the Riverlands; / On that rich region, base your own royal stand.' . . ."

cards.name: Zodiac Ox
cards.text: Swampwalk (This creature can't be blocked as long as defending player controls a Swamp.)
cards.flavor: ". . . Cao's abdication changed the face of all; / No mighty battles marked the Southland's fall. . . ."

cards.name: Zodiac Pig
cards.text: Swampwalk (This creature can't be blocked as long as defending player controls a Swamp.)

cards.name: Jakub Šlemr Bio (1999)
cards.text: 1997 World Champion Jakub Šlemr came within two matches of becoming the first person to repeat as World Champion. The 22-year-old Prague native earned a flawless 6—0 resord during the Standard portion of the Swiss rounds. Šlemr, along with fellow teammate and quarterfinalist Gary Wise, played a mono-black deck coined "Black Control." He used discard effects early with cards like Ravenous Rats, Duress, and Stupor. However, the majority of his deck was dedicated to board control with Cursed Scrolls, Powder Kegs, and Phyrexian Plaguelords.

cards.name: Kai Budde Bio
cards.text: Known as the "King of the Grand Prix," Kai Budde earned an unprecedented three Grand Prix titles in 1999. Though he went only 4—2 during the Swiss portion of the World Championships, he cruised through the Final 8 to become the 1999 World Champion. The 19-year-old Köln, Germany native played a red-artifact deck that contained more than 30 artifacts. He used those artifacts to quickly generate huge amounts of mana, with which he could play a big creature like Masticore or Covetous Dragon. He would then finish off his opponent with a well-timed Wildfire.

cards.name: Mark Le Pine Bio
cards.text: Though only 17 years old, New Hampshire—native Mark Le Pine is a Pro Tour veteran. He has been with the Pro Tour since Atlanta '96 and has made the Top 8 three times (Mainz '97, Rome '98, and Worlds '99). Le Pine played an aggressive red deck called "Sped Red." With his deck he applied pressure early with 11 fast creatures, then he'd shift into land-destruction mode with Wasteland, Stone Rain, Pillage, and Avalanche Riders. For the late game Le Pine used Cursed Scroll and Hammer of Bogardan to finish off his mana-crippled opponent.

cards.name: Matt Linde Bio
cards.text: Semifinalist Matt Linde is no stranger to high-level Magic® competition. The 18-year-old Maryland native was the 1998 U.S. National Champion. Linde played a very fast mono-green "Stompy" deck with 26 creatures—24 of which cost two mana or less to play. Supplementing this furious creature assault were four Rancors and four Giant Growths. Though the deck was designed to win by turn five, it did feature four Cursed Scrolls in case the game dragged on.

cards.name: Janosch Kühn Bio (2000)
cards.text: Hannover, Germany native Janosch Kühn joined an elite group of players in earning his second World Championship Top 8. Kühn played a red-green deck known as "Angry 'Derm" or "Son of Hermit." The deck built up its mana early with Birds of Paradise or Llanowar Elves, and then followed that up with mana-denial cards like Stone Rain, Plow Under, and Avalanche Riders. Masticore and Blastoderm provided the finishing punch.

cards.name: Jon Finkel Bio
cards.text: "World Champion" was the one honor Jon Finkel had yet to claim. His dominating performance at this year's World Championships earned him that title at last. Finkel played an explosive deck that is named after its most important card, Tinker. Fellow Team Antarctica member Dan O'Mahoney-Schwartz designed this monoblue deck. The deck used artifacts such as Grim Monolith, Metalworker, and Voltaic Key to quickly generate huge amounts of mana, and then used that mana to put large creatures into play.

cards.name: Nicolas Labarre Bio
cards.text: The 2000 World Championships was Nicolas Labarre's third Top 8 finish at a Pro Tour™ event (Rome '98, New York '99, Worlds '00). This Rennes, France native played a combo deck that he called "Chimera." This deck used searching cards like Academy Rector and Enlightened Tutor to fetch Fecundity, Saproling Cluster, and Ashnod's Altar. Once those three cards were in play, Labarre could generate as much mana as he wanted. With unlimited mana, he could play a very big Blaze or use Whetstone to immediately deck his opponent.

cards.name: Tom van de Logt Bio (2000)
cards.text: Quarterfinalist Tom van de Logt posted a perfect 6—0 record during the Standard portion of this year's World Championships. The 19-year-old Groesbeek, Holland native was playing a deck that had a big impact on the metagame this year, "Replenish." This deck used cards like Attunement and Frantic Search to put powerful enchantments, such as Parallax Wave and Opalescence, into the graveyard and then used Replenish to put them all back into play at once.

cards.name: Alex Borteh Bio
cards.text: Eighteen-year-old Alex Borteh came on strong in the last half of the 2000—2001 Pro Tour™ season. He posted an impressive Top 8 finish at U.S. Nationals and followed that up by coming within one match of winning this year's Worlds. The soon-to-be Ohio State University freshman played a monoblue combo deck that he liked to call "Da Folk." This deck wins by using Opposition and Static Orb to establish a lock down while legions of Merfolk overrun opponents' immobilized defenses.

cards.name: Antoine Ruel Bio
cards.text: A member of the famous Team Block Ops, Antoine Ruel, a native of Aubervilliers, France, took his blue-black-red control deck to a third-place finish at this year's World Championships. Ruel credits his teammate Laurent Pagorek for the deck that he calls "AK-Go." The deck, which Ruel played to a 5—1 record during the Standard portion of the tournament, relies on card drawing (most notably Accumulated Knowledge, or "AK" for short), countermagic ("Go," for short), red for board control, and Nether Spirits for the win.

cards.name: Jan Tomcani Bio
cards.text: Jan Tomcani, from Bratislava in the Slovak Republic, came out of nowhere to stun everyone by posting a perfect 6—0 record in the Standard portion of this year's Worlds. Tomcani then proved that his run was no fluke by working his way up to the quarterfinals, where he lost to Alex Borteh in a close five-game match. Tomcani played a version of "Fires," the green-red deck that defined much of this year's metagame. Tomcani's version, which splashed black, follows the normal Fires archetype of playing cheap creatures followed by Fires of Yavimaya and big creatures like Blastoderm or Spiritmonger.

cards.name: Tom van de Logt Bio (2001)
cards.text: Tom van de Logt is the 2001 Netherlands National Champion as well as one of an elite group of players who have posted back-to-back World Championship Top 8 performances. Currently a student in Groesbeek, van de Logt posted an impressive 5—1 record in the Standard portion of this year's Worlds. He described his aggressive black-red "Machine Head" deck as "the deck that beats the deck that beats 'Fires.'" He liked the explosive "I win" draws that his deck provided, and he especially liked the way it performed against blue decks.

cards.name: Brian Kibler Bio
cards.text: Pro Tour™ veteran Brian Kibler piloted his green-white-red "Red Zone 2K2" deck to an impressive finish at this year's Worlds. This deck quickly tried to put its many creatures into the "red zone," the attacking zone on the playmats used on the Pro Tour circuit. The twenty-one—year-old Kibler attends Emory University in Atlanta, Georgia, and is part of the "Mini Colony" playtest group that designed the Red Zone 2K2 deck.

cards.name: Carlos Romão Bio
cards.text: Carlos Romão played the same style of deck that many people at this year's World Championships chose to play: blue-black Psychatog. He simply played his version better than everyone else playing theirs. Romão, known as "Jaba" to his friends, was a perfect 6-0 during the Swiss portion of the tournament, posting a stunning 12-0 game record. This twenty-year-old native of São Paulo, Brazil, has been widely regarded as one of the best players in South America. His deck tried to stay alive long enough to play Upheaval, while floating mana to replay Psychatog on the same turn.

cards.name: Raphael Levy Bio
cards.text: A native of Toulouse, France, Raphael Levy posted an impressive 5-1 record during the Standard portion of this year's Worlds playing a blue-green deck he named "Le Wonder Goose." This deck used lots of small creatures—like Numble Mongoose and Werebear—that get bigger at threshold. The deck used blue not for countermagic, but for cards like Careful Study and Mental Note, which help the deck reach threshold more quickly, and for Wonder in the graveyard, which allows the deck's pumped-up threshold creatures to fly.

cards.name: Sim Han How Bio
cards.text: Malaysian National Champion Sim Han How raised some eyebrows by posting a 6-0 record with his blue-green-red "Squirrel Opposition" deck. This deck tried to get out lots of Squirrel tokens with Squirrel Nest before using Opposition to tie up the opponent's creatures and mana. Han How won quite a few games using some tricky sideboarding, such as pulling out his enchantments and bringing in more beatdown cards like Flametongue Kavu and Roar of the Wurm. Besides being a top Magic® player, Han How is also a student at Bandar Utama College in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia.

cards.name: Daniel Zink Bio
cards.text: Daniel Zink, a student from Bochum, Germany, players the control deck that defined this year's World Championships. The white-blue-green "Wake" deck is named after the powerful enchantment that's the heart of the deck. Once Mirari's Wake is in play, the deck produces more mana, draws more cards, counters more spells, and makes more Soldiers than opponents can possibly handle. Zink had help from fellow German and 2002-2003 Player of the Year Kai Budde in adapting the "Wake" deck to the post—Eigth Edition environment.

cards.name: Dave Humpherys Bio
cards.text: The Top 8 is familiar territory for professional Magic player Dave Humpherys. With over $130,000 in career winnings and a Pro Tour championship on his resume, "The Hump" advanced to the Worlds semifinals for the second year in a row where he lost to eventual champion Daniel Zink. The blue-green madness deck he played has been a Standard mainstay for more than a year. It revolves around Torment madness cards like Basking Rootwalla and Circular Logic, together with discard-enablers like Aquamoeba and Wild Mongrel. Humpherys, who recently earned his Ph.D. from MIT, credits this version of the deck to Norway's Sigurd Eskeland.

cards.name: Peer Kröger Bio
cards.text: Hometown hero Peer Kröger played his own version of the classic "Reanimator" deck to an impressive record during this year's World Championships. The twenty-eight-year-old communications and computer science student nicknamed his deck "Herbert Wise" after the famous H. P. Lovecraft work "Herbert Wise—Reanimator." Winning with this deck is a two-step process: Step 1. Use Entomb or Buried Alive to quickly get daunting creatures into the graveyard. Step 2. Bring the creature back to life with Zombify or Doomed Necromancer. The mostly black deck also uses Burning Wish to find just the right answers to deal with opponents' plans.

cards.name: Wolfgang Eder Bio
cards.text: Wolfgang Eder introduced this black-red "Goblin Bidding" deck to the world at this year's European Championships. The twenty-two-year-old student from Weinheim, Germany, says the inspiration for the deck came from trying to give the typical Goblin tribe something to do in the midgame. He achieved this by adding black to the deck for Patriarch's Bidding, which brings every Goblin in the graveyard back to play. And with cards like Goblin Warchief and Siege-Gang Commander, those Goblins have haste and bring friends with them! A resolved Patriarch's Bidding is usually game over.

cards.name: Aeo Paquette Bio
cards.text: Professional Magic® player Aeo Paquette played the deck that defined the metagame at the 2004 World Championships: "Affinity." Against a field full of decks designed to beat Affinity, this nineteen-year-old Canadian piloted his fast beatdown deck to a 5—1 record during the Standard portion of the tournament. Paquette credits his friend Jeff Cunningham for helping him design an Affinity deck that could compete so well against the field.

cards.name: Gabriel Nassif Bio
cards.text: Twenty-year-old Gabriel Nassif is considered to be the best player never to have won a Pro Tour™ event. Designed to beat the ubiquitous "Affinity" decks, his blue-white control deck also plays well against anti-Affinity decks. Worlds marked the third time in the season that the Parisian had made it to the final day of a Pro Tour event, and his performance earned Nassif the coveted 2004 Player of the Year award—a title he will defend vigorously next year.

cards.name: Julien Nuijten Bio
cards.text: The youngest ever Magic® World Champion, Dutch wunderkind Julien Nuijten came out of nowhere to stun the field. Just fifteen years old, Nuijten proved that he can play with the best. Playing a green—white Astral Slide deck designed to destroy "Affinity", he posted a respectable 4-2 record on the Standard day at Worlds and then calmly swept the field on the final day. He says the inspiration for his deck came from an Internet article by Pro Tour™ veteran Brian Kibler.

cards.name: Manuel Bevand Bio
cards.text: Pro Tour™ veteran Manuel Bevand played an artifact-based combo deck to a perfect 6-0 record on the Standard day at Worlds. His deck uses Krark-Clan Ironworks to quickly get a Myr Incubator into play, which then creates thirty or more 1/1 Myr creatures—sometimes as early as the third turn! A twenty-seven-year-old freelance game designer from Paris, France, Bevand has been a Magic® regular since 1994, playing in over a dozen Pro Tour events. He credits Magic Online for getting him back into championship form.

Whenever enchanted creature attacks or blocks, its controller loses 3 life.

cards.flavor: "Wisdom is not the counting of all the drops in a waterfall. Wisdom is learning why the water seeks the earth."

cards.name: Crafty Pathmage

cards.flavor:
Follow the pathmage
—Otarian expression meaning "escape quickly"

cards.name: Dehydration

Enchanted creature doesn't untap during its controller's untap step.

cards.name: Deluge

"From the sea came all life, and to the sea it will return. The sooner the better."
—Emperor Aboshan

cards.name: Discombobulate

"I said 'pick his brain,' not 'tear off his head.'"
—Riptide Project researcher

cards.name: Duct Crawler

cards.flavor:
"Boss told us to try and train 'em. Trained it to attack—it ate Flugg. Trained it to run fast—it got away. Success!"
—Dlig, goblin spelunker

cards.name: Elven Riders

"For what are leaves but countless blades

"Bet you can't put it through the eye."
"Left or right?"

cards.name: Starlight Invoker

"Once you create perfection, what else is there to make?"

"Some say it's better to think before you act. While those people are considering all the options, that's usually when I kill them."

"We're not sure what one looks like, so to be safe, nobody look at anything until we're out of here."

"Their buzzing makes my bones hum from a mile away."
—Galenti, treasure hunter

cards.name: Treetop Bracers

Enchant creature (Target a creature as you cast this. This card enters attached to that creature.)
Enchanted creature gets +1/+1 and can't be blocked except by creatures with flying.
